grand_strategy.reading:
Egypt is a state that sells its position. It cannot feed, fuel or finance itself,
so the strategy of the Sisi regime is to be too central to be allowed to fail:
the Suez Canal and the Rafah crossing, the Gaza table, the Arab League seat,
a Mediterranean liquefaction hub, an army that can be lent to the Gulf. Each
of the payers is a different patron (the IMF and the EU for the
balance sheet, the Gulf for cash, Washington for the army, Paris and Berlin for
the equipment, Moscow for the nuclear plant, Beijing for industry) and the cost
is that none of them is aligned with the others on Sudan, Israel or Iran. The year
2026 widened every gap at once: the US-Iran war doubled the energy bill and put
Egyptian jets on Emirati soil while Cairo called itself neutral; the Israeli gas
that was meant to be the bridge is the lever Jerusalem uses against the Sinai
buildup; the Houthis, not Egypt, decide whether the canal pays; and the Nile has
turned from a water dispute into a Horn-wide alliance contest with Ethiopia in civil
war. The Luttwak reading is that Egypt's moves are rational at each level and
self-defeating across levels: tactical gains (a summit, a deposit, a contract) are
paid for by a strategic dependency that will be called in when the IMF programme
ends in December 2026. Gaps in this card: Jordan, Iraq, India, the UK, Djibouti, and
the status of Tiran and Sanafir were not researched (no source retrieved).
